subject: Food Science
title: Pulsed Electric Fields
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pulsed Electric Fields.

hook.text: Zap juice with 40,000 volts for microseconds and bacteria die—but the juice stays raw, uncooked, and full of vitamins.

buildup.text: Pulsed electric field (PEF) technology creates pores in microbial cell membranes through electrical pulses. Cells leak and die.

discovery.text: PEF-treated juice retains 95% of vitamin C versus 70% for thermally pasteurized juice—better nutrition, same safety.

twist.text: PEF also tenderizes meat by disrupting muscle cell membranes. One technology, two completely different applications.

climax.text: Energy cost is 80% lower than thermal pasteurization. Faster, cheaper, and better quality—adoption is growing rapidly.

punchline.text: Electricity punches holes in bacteria. Vitamins pass through unharmed.

quiz.question: How does PEF technology kill bacteria?
options: Electrical pulses create pores in cell membranes, causing cells to die
